items.title: 13.11 Use of chlorine in water purification

blocks.text: Chlorine gas is very poisonous, but in small quantities it is harmless to humans and poisonous to the bacteria that cause disease. Because of its strong disinfectant properties chlorine is widely used in treatment plants to purify water: chlorine is added to water, where it forms active species that kill bacteria and other pathogens. Swimming pool water is chlorinated with slightly higher concentrations because it is likely to carry more bacteria. The primary active species are chloric(I) acid or hypochlorous acid, HOCl, and the chlorate(I) or hypochlorite ion, OCl-. Chlorination is a relatively inexpensive method of water disinfection.

blocks.caption: Chlorination at a glance
rows: small doses harmless to people, lethal to pathogens; cheap
water treatment plants; swimming pools at a slightly higher dose

blocks.prompt: Describe one significant disadvantage of using chlorine in water purification (exercise Q.2l).
blocks.explanation: Chlorine reacts with organic matter in the water to form chlorinated by-products such as trihalomethanes, some of which are suspected carcinogens, and it leaves a taste and smell; chlorine gas itself is toxic and must be handled and stored with care.

items: Chlorine disinfects water cheaply: small doses kill pathogens; active species HOCl and OCl-; pools get a higher dose.
